name: MK-3984
lead: MK-3984 is an experimental selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) targeting muscle and bone tissue.[2] Very little published information exists: it is mentioned in the SARM literature [1] and has been the subject of a 2026 doping-control study of its metabolism in zebrafish.[2]
No clinical trials or human data were found, and it is not approved for any use.

paras: No studies found. A review of SARMs for cancer-related muscle wasting discusses the drug class, and a laboratory study mapped the compound's metabolites in zebrafish, identifying 82 metabolites and 12 metabolic pathways, with reductive defluorination dominating phase I metabolism.[1][2]
The metabolite study was aimed at doping control, indicating interest in detecting the compound.[2] The sources reviewed do not document use of MK-3984 in looksmaxxing communities.

quick.overview:
MK-3984 is a little-documented SARM candidate aimed at muscle and bone. The only dedicated study found maps its metabolism in zebrafish for doping control.

No human trials were found.
quick.mechanism: As a SARM it is designed to act on androgen receptors in muscle and bone, though no mechanism data specific to it were found.
quick.risks: Human safety is unknown, and it is not approved for any use.
